issues.title: Incorrect Gaussian-mixture change of variables
issues.failure_explanation: With eta=u^2/2 and x=uv, the two quadratic terms in eq:gibbs become v^2 and beta^2 lambda^2 u^2/4, rather than beta lambda(v^2+u^2)/2. Hence the displayed change of variables does not supply the stated lifted density and leaves the only given derivation supporting thm:overparam invalid. Setting eta=u^2/(lambda beta) matches both coefficients and yields the required Jacobian factor proportional to u.
issues.overall_effect: The projection theorem is mathematically salvageable, but its stated Gaussian-mixture derivation is incorrect as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the asserted substitution by η_i=u_i²/(βλ). Add the coordinatewise check that the two quadratic terms become βλ(v_i²+u_i²)/2 and that η_i^{-1/2}|∂(η_i,x_i)/∂(u_i,v_i)| is proportional to u_i; tracking the constants then proves thm:overparam, including its normalization identity.
issues.why_classification: The wrong substitution makes the paper's sole stated derivation invalid, so this is not merely a transcriptional typo. Nevertheless, the correction is uniquely forced by eq:gibbs and pi and requires only a short coefficient-and-Jacobian calculation, preserving the theorem exactly without a new lemma or mathematical loss.

issues.title: Pointwise radial-density misidentification
issues.failure_explanation: For cylindrical p and u_i=(y_i^2+z_i^2)^{1/2}, the pushforward density with respect to du dv is rho(u,v)=(2pi)^d(prod_i u_i)p(y,z,v), not p(y,z,v). The old proof establishes that the radial projection solves the same SDE and hence has the same law, but that does not support the stated pointwise density equality.
issues.overall_effect: The final density clause of wp is false, and the bounded-G entropy proof later uses the same false equality p=rho. The well-posedness, positivity, and law-level radial construction are not defeated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace agree by the radial pushforward formula ρ(t,u,v)=(2π)^d(∏_i u_i)p(t,y,z,v), or state the equivalent law-level assertion. In thm_bndd_G, let the Cartesian invariant density be q; its radial pushforward satisfies π(u,v)=(2π)^d(∏_i u_i)q(y,z,v). Hence ρ/π=p/q, and polar integration gives H(ρ_t|π)=H(p_t|q), including at time zero, so the same entropy rate follows.
issues.why_classification: The proof uses a genuinely false density equality, so the issue is substantive rather than a typo. The missing polar Jacobian and the resulting entropy cancellation are, however, short routine local calculations that preserve wp's law-level result and the exact entropy theorem and rate.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: If the initial distribution is cylindrical, the marginal distribution of $((y_t^2+z_t^2)^{1/2},v_t)$ equals the law of the solution $(u_t,v_t)$ of \cref{main}.

issues.title: Unsupported high-order inverse-time moments
issues.failure_explanation: Corollary part 2 claims finiteness for every q>=1. BDG actually gives an expectation of (int u^{2epsilon-2})^{q/2}; the old proof instead bounds it by (int E[u^{2epsilon-2}])^{q/2}. Jensen supplies that upper bound only for q<=2, so the argument establishes only a materially smaller moment range and not the stated high-order moments.
issues.overall_effect: The high-q part of the integrated inverse-moment corollary and the corresponding all-q time-regularity assertion are unsupported. The later finite-time error argument uses low moments, so its relevant use can survive the range restriction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict part 2 of cor to 1≤q<2 and impose the same range on the q-dependent time-regularity assertion in timeregbnd. Use BDG followed by the concave-power Jensen bound valid in that range, and check the finite-time numerical proof using these results with exponents below two; its convergence conclusion can then remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old estimate does not support the advertised all-q moment guarantee, and reducing all moments to a bounded moment range is a meaningful weakening, so a minor same-guarantee repair is unavailable. The same additive functional and time-regularity conclusions survive on a substantial range, and the downstream finite-time convergence argument only needs that range, making this a contained, limited-loss repair rather than a serious reconstruction.

issues.title: Malformed Novikov–Girsanov measure change
issues.failure_explanation: For the diffusion coefficient sqrt(2/beta), the Girsanov integrand must be the scaled vector sqrt(beta/2)b and must be integrated against dW. The old expression instead contains int b(z_t)dt, which is vector-valued and cannot define the asserted positive martingale. Moreover, if this subsection is read as an independent construction of z, evaluating the density along the not-yet-constructed target process is circular. Thus the claimed Girsanov implication to positivity is not established by the displayed measure change.
issues.overall_effect: The alternative Girsanov proof of positivity and well-posedness is invalid as written. The earlier theorem wp independently establishes the process and positivity, and the later strong-Feller argument uses the exponential-integrability part rather than this malformed density.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Set θ(z)=√(β/2)b(z) and explicitly use the process already supplied by wp. Replace the malformed expression by the stochastic exponential exp(-∫_0^T θ(z_s)·dW_s−(1/2)∫_0^T‖θ(z_s)‖²ds). Novikov makes this a positive mean-one density; under the equivalent measure, W^Q=W+∫θds and the b-drift is removed, giving the decoupled CIR/OU process. Its non-hitting property therefore transfers back to z, and a countable union over integer T gives positivity for all times.
issues.why_classification: The missing stochastic integral, diffusion scaling, and measure-change direction invalidate the inference, so this is not a typo. They are repaired by a standard local Girsanov calculation already supported by the exponential-integrability estimate and the preceding construction; no dependent result, rate, or substantive guarantee must be weakened.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: $M_T = \exp(\int_0^T b(\hat z_t) \cdot dW_t - \frac12 \int_0^T b(\hat z_t)^2 dt)$

issues.title: Incorrect Riemannian correction drift
issues.failure_explanation: For the displayed M and H, subtracting -M grad H from the Itô drift mu gives Gamma=(1/2)(3·1_d,x/eta). The old proof instead asserts (1/2)(1_d,x/eta), even though its subsequent Fokker–Planck expansion contains the vector (3/2,x/(2eta)). Thus the transformed SDE is not the Riemannian equation stated under the old divergence convention; the computation supports the revised coordinate-divergence correction.
issues.overall_effect: The standalone identification of the transformed HLD as the stated Riemannian Langevin diffusion is wrong. The original HLD, its invariant density, and the later ergodicity and discretization results do not use this identification.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the old metric-divergence correction by the coordinate-divergence correction appropriate to the stated density relative to Lebesgue measure: Γ_j(z)=∑_k ∂_{z_k}M_{jk}(z). Direct differentiation gives Γ=(1/2)(3·1_d,x/η), so the transformed drift satisfies μ=-M∇H+Γ and the displayed Fokker–Planck identity remains valid.
issues.why_classification: The old proof uses the wrong divergence convention and therefore makes a genuine false identification, rather than a purely typographical coefficient error. Correcting the convention and differentiating the displayed matrix are short local computations that preserve the same transformed SDE, target density, and standalone Riemannian interpretation, with no downstream loss.

issues.title: Dropped drift-noise term in discrete path moments
issues.failure_explanation: After expanding the squared u-update, the old proof displays the nonnegative term 2B sqrt(2/beta) Delta t ||v^k|| ||Delta W_k^1|| and drops it without compensation. Because ass:2 concerns an expected path supremum, taking expectations at a single step does not remove this term; its signed precursor must be retained as a martingale and treated with a maximal inequality. Consequently the proof that reg3 implies ass:2 is incomplete.
issues.overall_effect: The old derivation does not discharge ass:2, so the finite-time convergence theorem under reg3 lacks its stated moment input. The invariant-measure theorem also uses that finite-time result, although it has the independent non-uniformity defect represented by C02.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the signed drift-noise cross terms and combine them with the existing noise martingale. With h=Δt, use increments proportional to ⟨u^k-hv^k⊙∇G(u^k⊙v^k),ΔW_k^1⟩+⟨v^k-hu^k⊙∇G(u^k⊙v^k),ΔW_k^2⟩. These are martingale differences, and boundedness of ∇G bounds their predictable quadratic variation by C h(1+h²B²)‖(u,v)^k‖². The maximal BDG estimate, Young absorption, and the discrete Gronwall step already used in the proof then yield the required expected path-supremum moments and restore the missing input to the listed dependent results.
issues.why_classification: Dropping the nonnegative bound is an invalid inference, so the defect is not a typo. A complete repair is nevertheless short and routine: the old proof already invokes BDG for the adjacent martingale, and only its predictable coefficient and quadratic-variation bound need to be corrected. This preserves all assumptions and conclusions without new proof architecture or weakening.

issues.title: Non-uniform use of finite-time convergence for invariant laws

failure_location.quote: If $\pi_\tstep$ does not satisfy \cref{reg3}, we may replace $\pi_\tstep$ with  a regularised distribution $\tilde \pi_\tstep$

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem claims convergence of pi_Delta t to pi for every Lipschitz test function. The finite-time theorem it invokes assumes an initial law satisfying reg3(ii), whereas the proposed initial laws tilde pi_Delta t vary with Delta t. Restricting pi_Delta t to a growing ball gives tail closeness but does not prove a uniformly bounded ratio tilde pi_Delta t/pi or uniform finite-time constants. Thus the asserted limit E_{1,T}(Delta t)->0 does not follow. The new proof uses rho_0=pi, whose ratio to pi is exactly one, and a discrete contraction uniform in physical time.
issues.overall_effect: The old proof does not establish convergence of the discretized invariant measures, one of the paper's principal numerical conclusions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the non-uniform regularization argument by a step-size-uniform long-time analysis of the discrete chain. Establish uniform Lyapunov and higher-moment bounds together with a coupling or minorization over ⌈t_0/Δt⌉ steps, yielding a weighted-TV or Wasserstein contraction in physical time with constants independent of Δt. Then start both dynamics from π, for which ρ_0/π=1, and use W_1(π_Δt,π)≤W_1(π_Δt,P_Δt^kπ)+W_1(P_Δt^kπ,P_Tπ): the first term decays uniformly as T grows and the second tends to zero for fixed T by finite-time convergence, while P_Tπ=π.
issues.why_classification: Truncating π_Δt controls only tails and supplies neither a uniform density ratio nor uniform finite-time constants, so the asserted limit cannot be recovered by a local edit. Dropping the invariant-law theorem or making it conditional on the missing uniform control would entail major loss. The concrete same-guarantee repair requires new uniform escape, coupling/minorization, higher-moment, and contraction arguments across the discrete long-time theory, which is essentially new global proof architecture and therefore serious.
